A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same work, Emergent Response Planning in LLMs, with all 20 pages and Appendices A–B available. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original probing experiments across six response-attribute tasks, cross-dataset evaluations, and ablations in Sections 4–5, with extended regression results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the original empirical results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix B, including prediction scores, model-scaling analyses, and generation-time probing.

M1.justification: The probing procedure, one-hidden-layer MLP architecture, regression and classification losses, representation inputs, and greedy response generation are identical in Section 3 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six tasks using the same twelve datasets, including the same within-dataset, cross-dataset, and generation-time scenarios. Sections 3–5 and Appendix A contain no coverage changes.

E2.justification: The random baselines in Figures 2–3 and verbalized Self-Estimate comparisons in Figure 8 are unchanged. The same model sets participate in the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Both versions specify the same 60:20:20 split, 400 training epochs, hidden-size and layer searches, correlation and F1 metrics, and greedy decoding. Appendix A retains identical filtering, augmentation, and split-grouping procedures.

E4.justification: The hidden-size, layer-wise, model-scaling, generation-position, and self-estimation analyses in Figures 4–8 are identical. No ablation, robustness analysis, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 3.3 retains averaging across three random seeds. Error bars and plus-minus annotations throughout the main and appendix figures are unchanged, with no added uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings match, including Appendix B. For example, Qwen2-7B-Instruct response-length Spearman correlation remains 0.85±0.00 within-dataset and 0.64±0.02 cross-dataset in Figures 9–10.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of the attribute rule, probing criterion, task, and collected dataset in Section 3 are identical. Neither version adds or revises a theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about emergent planning of structure, content, and behavior attributes, the proposed formal framework, and potential generation-control applications.

C2.justification: Interpretations of generalization, representation hierarchy, scaling, and generation dynamics are unchanged. Section 6 and the conclusion retain the same sampling qualifications, shortcut discussion, and unresolved causal-mechanism questions.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix A retain identical hyperparameters, model and dataset access links, prompt templates, labeling rules, and representation-collection instructions. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are identical. The positioning relative to hidden-representation probing and prior look-ahead research, including the novelty claim, remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2, dated 6 Jun 2025, to v3, dated 4 Aug 2025. The title, authors, prose, headings, section order, and appendix organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–10, appendix tables, captions, axes, legends, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages match outside the updated first-page arXiv stamp text.

improvement.justification: The main text and appendices retain identical methods, evidence, claims, limitations, and reproducibility information. The administrative arXiv stamp update produces no meaningful difference in the paper's overall quality.
